text: A song of ascents. Of David. If the LORD had not been on our side—let Israel say it—
if the LORD had not been on our side when people rose against us,
then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger blazed against us.

versions.text: they would have swallowed us alive, so fiercely did their anger burn against us.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew opens with אֲזַי ("then"), which links this verse to the conditional clauses of vv. 1–2 and carries the same force in vv. 4–5. Also, בַּחֲרוֹת אַפָּם is a temporal/circumstantial clause ("when their anger burned"), not an expression of degree; "so fiercely did" adds an intensity not in the text.

text: Then the waters would have swept us away, the torrent would have gone over us;

versions.text: The waters would have engulfed us, the torrent would have swept over us;
versions.explanation: The repeated אֲזַי ("then") is part of the psalm's deliberate threefold rhythm (vv. 3, 4, 5) and reads well aloud; restoring it keeps the parallel structure. "Swept us away" also matches שָׁטַף more closely and avoids using "swept" twice in the same line.

text: over us would have swept the raging waters.
Blessed be the LORD, who did not give us up as prey to their teeth.
We have escaped like a bird from the fowler's snare; the snare is broken, and we have escaped.
Our help is in the name of the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
